changes.answer: Wrangler no longer supports service environments: the `legacy_env` field and `--legacy-env` flag are gone (the field now raises an error) and every environment deploys as its own Worker named <name>-<environment>.
changes.primary_quote: The "legacy_env" field is no longer supported, so please remove it from your configuration file.
changes.signal_reason: A user-authored config that still sets legacy_env fails validation with an error telling you to remove the field.
changes.notes: Docs (workers/wrangler/environments/) only say each environment deploys as <top-level-name>-<environment-name>; they no longer mention legacy_env, so the source at wrangler@4.148.0 is the primary. Same error text continues: 'Service environments have been removed, and each environment is now deployed as its own Worker named "<name>-<environment>".' The hidden --legacy-env flag exists in src/deploy/index.ts and src/dev.ts at wrangler@4.110.0 and is gone at 4.148.0. Exception: redirected configs generated by tools (e.g. older Vite plugin) have the field silently stripped instead of erroring.

changes.answer: To turn Node.js compatibility off on a compatibility date of 2026-08-04 or later, set both `no_nodejs_compat` and `no_nodejs_compat_v2` flags.
changes.primary_quote: To turn off Node.js compatibility completely with a compatibility date of 2026-08-04 or later, remove the positive flags if present. Then add both no_nodejs_compat and no_nodejs_compat_v2.
changes.signal_reason: A config that simply omits nodejs_compat now gets Node.js compatibility switched on by the compatibility date, with no error.
changes.notes: Same page: 'For compatibility dates of 2026-08-04 or later, Workers enables both nodejs_compat and nodejs_compat_v2 by default.' Also stated on workers/configuration/compatibility-flags/.

changes.answer: `wrangler deploy --latest` and `wrangler versions upload --latest` set the compatibility date to the newest date the bundled workerd supports (its release date).
changes.primary_quote: Use the latest compatibility date supported by this version of Wrangler
changes.signal_reason: The flag still works but yields the workerd release date (e.g. 2026-10-06 in 4.148.0) rather than today; only a warning is logged.
changes.notes: deploy-args.ts defines the shared `latest` arg for both 'deploy' and 'versions upload' and logs 'Using the latest compatibility date supported by this version of Wrangler (${DEFAULT_COMPAT_DATE})'. packages/workers-utils/src/default-compat-date.ts: DEFAULT_COMPAT_DATE 'is the release date of the `workerd` version pinned in the pnpm catalog'. The docs page workers/wrangler/commands/workers/ matches for versions upload but its deploy section still shows the stale text 'Use the latest version of the Workers runtime.' (default: true), so source is used.

changes.answer: Setting `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off Wrangler telemetry, regardless of other telemetry settings.
changes.primary_quote: DO_NOT_TRACK=1 takes precedence over all other telemetry settings.
changes.signal_reason: additive: code written for the old behavior keeps working and nothing errors; the old advice is just incomplete (wrangler telemetry disable and WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false still work).
changes.notes: Not on developers.cloudflare.com (system-environment-variables page lists only WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS). telemetry.md is the data-policy page the docs link to; quote is rendered from the raw markdown (backtick markup removed). Preceding line: 'Wrangler also honors the `DO_NOT_TRACK` environment variable. Set it to `1` to disable telemetry:'.

changes.answer: `wrangler d1 create <name> --jurisdiction us` creates a D1 database in the US jurisdiction.
changes.primary_quote: The location to restrict the D1 database to run and store data within to comply with local regulations. Note that if jurisdictions are set, the location hint is ignored. Options: eu: The European Union fedramp: FedRAMP-compliant data centers us: The United States
changes.signal_reason: additive: code written for the old behavior keeps working and nothing errors; the old advice is just incomplete.
changes.notes:
This text is the description of the --jurisdiction flag of d1 create (single

with line breaks, rendered as one line). d1/configuration/data-location/ also lists us = The United States under Supported jurisdictions. Jurisdiction can only be set at creation.

changes.answer: `wrangler dev` captures local traces and console logs into the Local Explorer Observability tab by default; set `X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=false` to opt out.
changes.primary_quote: Local Explorer automatically captures traces and logs from every Worker invocation during wrangler dev without modifying your code.
changes.signal_reason: Default changed: capture now happens without opting in; setting X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=true is harmless and nothing errors.
changes.notes: The opt-out is not in the docs; source packages/workers-utils/src/environment-variables/misc-variables.ts at wrangler@4.148.0: 'Defaults to `true` so the Local Explorer's Observability tab captures traces and logs out of the box. Set `X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=false` to opt out' (defaultValue: true).

changes.answer: Workers have a single 64 MiB uncompressed script size limit, and Wrangler's size warnings compare the uncompressed bundle against it.
changes.primary_quote: There is no compressed size limit. Only the uncompressed bundle size counts.
changes.signal_reason: Limits got looser; existing bundles still deploy and nothing errors, so the stale 3/10 MiB-gzip belief only misleads sizing decisions.
changes.notes: Limits table: 'Worker size (uncompressed) 64 MiB 64 MiB' for Free and Paid. Page also: 'The Total Upload value is your uncompressed bundle size. The gzip value is shown for reference but is not a limit.' Source packages/deploy-helpers/src/deploy/helpers/bundle-reporter.ts colors the 'Total Upload' line yellow/red at >70%/>90% of MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE_BYTES (64 MiB); that coloring is the 'warning'.

changes.answer: Deploys can choose a Durable Objects code update strategy (`--durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate` or `deferred <delay>`, or `durable_objects.code_update_strategy`); unset, it is deferred with a 5-minute maximum delay.
changes.primary_quote: The argument "--durable-objects-code-update-mode" must be either "immediate" or "deferred <duration>".
changes.signal_reason: Deploys without the flag now default to deferred (up to 300 s) code updates for running Durable Objects; nothing errors.
changes.notes: Same file: DEFAULT_DURABLE_OBJECTS_CODE_UPDATE_STRATEGY = { mode: 'deferred', max_delay: 300 }, resolved as flag ?? config code_update_strategy ?? default; delay max 24 h. workers-utils environment.ts: max_delay 'Defaults to 300 (5 minutes) and cannot exceed 86400 (24 hours).' Docs (workers/wrangler/commands/workers/, versions deploy) list the flag: 'How to update Durable Object code: immediate, or deferred followed by a maximum delay (for example, deferred 30s)' but not the default, so source is used.

changes.answer: R2 SQL, R2 Data Catalog and Pipelines commands now live under `wrangler basin sql`, `wrangler basin catalog` and `wrangler basin pipelines` and are stable; the old paths (`wrangler r2 sql`, `wrangler r2 bucket catalog`, `wrangler pipelines`) remain only as hidden aliases. Basin SQL reads its token from `WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` (falling back to `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`); `WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` is no longer read.
changes.primary_quote: Basin SQL expects the WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable to be set.
changes.signal_reason: Old command paths still run through hidden aliases; but scripts that set only WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN now fail with 'Missing WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN' unless CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is set.
changes.notes: Added the token rename the original answer missed. Docs: commands/r2/ documents 'npx wrangler basin sql query ...' and 'npx wrangler basin catalog enable <BUCKET_NAME>'; commands/pipelines/ is titled 'Basin Pipelines' with 'npx wrangler basin pipelines setup'. Source at wrangler@4.148.0 (and 4.145.0): basin/sql.ts r2SqlAlias = createAlias({ aliasOf: 'wrangler basin sql', metadata: { hidden: true } }); pipelines/index.ts pipelinesAlias aliasOf 'wrangler basin pipelines' hidden; namespaces status 'stable'. user/auth-variables.ts reads only WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN; wrangler@4.144.0 r2/sql.ts used WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN.

changes.answer: `wrangler check startup` is no longer alpha and reports bundle sizes plus a local timing summary.
changes.primary_quote: Analyze your Worker's startup phase. Wrangler reports bundle size and a summary of local CPU activity.
changes.signal_reason: additive: code written for the old behavior keeps working and nothing errors; the old advice is just incomplete (same command, more output).
changes.notes: Quote is the description under the 'check' > 'startup' heading; next line shows 'wrangler check startup' with sample output 'Bundle: ... Local startup profile: Profile window ... Active ... Idle'. Source src/check/commands.ts at wrangler@4.148.0: startup command metadata status 'stable' (the parent 'check' namespace is stable but hidden from help).

changes.answer: A Workflow's maximum number of concurrently running instances can be set with `workflows[].concurrency.limit` in the Wrangler config.
changes.primary_quote: "concurrency.limit" field must be a positive integer but got
changes.signal_reason: additive: code written for the old behavior keeps working and nothing errors; the old advice is just incomplete; without the field only account-level limits apply.
changes.notes: Not documented on developers.cloudflare.com (workflows/reference/limits and workers/wrangler/configuration show no per-workflow concurrency field). Source environment.ts at wrangler@4.148.0 defines on workflow bindings: 'concurrency?: { /** Maximum number of Workflow instances that can run concurrently */ limit?: number; }' and validation.ts validateWorkflowConcurrency ('Check the optional `concurrency` setting of a Workflow binding or export.') rejects non-positive-integer limits; only 'limit' is allowed inside 'concurrency'.

changes.answer: A `connect` config entry (e.g. `"connect": [{ "protocol": "tcp", "port": 5432 }]`) lets a Worker receive raw socket connections in its `connect(socket, env, ctx)` handler during local development (wrangler dev / Vite plugin): TCP since 4.125.0, and UDP (`protocol: "udp"`) since 4.139.0. It is experimental and local-only; deployed Workers cannot yet accept inbound sockets.
changes.primary_quote: Connect trigger — invokes this Worker's connect(socket, env, ctx) handler for raw socket connections received on the configured protocol/port.
changes.signal_reason: additive: code written for the old behavior keeps working and nothing errors; the old advice is just incomplete.
changes.notes: Original answer said TCP only; at wrangler@4.148.0 environment.ts types ConnectHandlerConfig as tcp | udp (udp adds idle_timeout_ms, max_pending_bytes) and validation.ts accepts 'protocol' 'tcp' or 'udp'. The docs quote is the generated reference for @cloudflare/config triggers.connect (packages/config/src/triggers.ts has the same text), which lowers to Wrangler's `connect` field; environment.ts: 'Specifies raw sockets that this Worker should listen on... delivers incoming connections directly to the Worker's `connect(socket, env, ctx)` handler.' workers/runtime-apis/tcp-sockets/ still says inbound TCP is 'coming soon' for deployed Workers. The `experimental` compatibility-flag requirement comes from the changelog (4.125.0); no Wrangler/Miniflare-side check was found, so it is presumably enforced by workerd.

changes.answer: Local testing endpoints moved to `/cdn-cgi/local/*` in Miniflare v5; wrangler dev rewrites the old `/cdn-cgi/*` paths so they still work.
changes.primary_quote: You can test the behavior of your scheduled() handler in local development by sending an HTTP request to /cdn-cgi/local/scheduled to trigger the handler.
changes.signal_reason: In wrangler dev and the Vite plugin the old /cdn-cgi/handler/* paths are transparently rewritten, so old requests still work (direct Miniflare v5 API users would see 404s).
changes.notes: Also workers/configuration/cron-triggers/: 'This exposes a /cdn-cgi/local/scheduled route...'; email local dev uses /cdn-cgi/local/email. Rewrite in source packages/wrangler/templates/startDevWorker/ProxyWorker.ts at wrangler@4.148.0: rewriteLegacyMiniflarePath with LEGACY_PATH_REWRITES (e.g. ['/cdn-cgi/explorer', '/cdn-cgi/local/explorer']), commented 'because wrangler cannot have a breaking change'.

changes.answer: Automatic resource provisioning on `wrangler deploy` is generally available (and now also covers Queue, Dispatch Namespace and Flagship bindings).
changes.primary_quote: Wrangler can automatically provision resources for you when you deploy your Worker without you having to create them ahead of time.
changes.signal_reason: additive: code written for the old behavior keeps working and nothing errors; the old advice is just incomplete; bindings without IDs are created on deploy by default.
changes.notes: Docs present it as a normal feature with no beta badge, and the next sentence lists coverage: 'This currently works for the following resources: KV, R2, D1, Flagship, AI Search, Agent Memory, Dispatch Namespaces and Queues.' The docs do not use the words 'generally available'; the source still has a hidden, default-on flag described 'Experimental: Enable automatic resource provisioning' (--experimental-provision / --x-provision) in src/index.ts at wrangler@4.148.0.

changes.answer: `wrangler versions secret bulk` deletes a secret when its value is `null` in the JSON input.
changes.primary_quote: Set a key to null in the JSON file to delete it. Deletion is not supported with .env files.
changes.signal_reason: additive: code written for the old behavior keeps working and nothing errors; the old advice is just incomplete (versions secret delete still works).
changes.notes: Quote is from the [FILE] arg description of versions secret bulk at wrangler@4.148.0; handler checks 'if (value === null)'. JSON only, not .env. The docs (commands/workers/) describe null-deletion for 'wrangler secret bulk' (since 4.97.0) but the 'versions secret bulk' section is still stale ('Create or update a secret variable for a Worker'), so source is used.

changes.answer: The `agents/channels` entry point is gone; Channels now lives under `agents/experimental/channels` (Slack, Telegram and Email under its subpaths) and is experimental.
changes.primary_quote: import { ChannelGateway, Channels } from "agents/experimental/channels";
changes.signal_reason: Importing the removed `agents/channels` subpath fails module resolution.
changes.notes: README code block at the tag (rendered verbatim) also shows agents/experimental/channels/email, /slack, /telegram. packages/agents/package.json exports at the tag list ./experimental/channels* and no ./channels entry. No prose docs page covers Channels in the agents package; the Think Channels page is a different API (configureChannels).

changes.answer: `npx agents tui <url>` opens a terminal client for an agent conversation's Web Channel.
changes.primary_quote: tui <url>   Chat with an agent's Web Channel from the terminal
changes.signal_reason: Additive command: following the stale answer breaks nothing; the user just misses the client.
changes.notes: Not in the docs; source at the tag (usage string in the CLI entry). package.json bin maps agents -> ./dist/cli.js. tui/args.ts usage: 'Usage: agents tui <url> [--as <participant>] [--header <name=value>]...'. It lives under experimental/channels/web/tui. Invoked as `npx agents tui <url>`.

changes.answer: Native RPC to async Agent/Think methods first runs lifecycle initialization, so Agents must be addressed by name; stubs from `newUniqueId()` or `idFromString()` fail their first async RPC.
changes.primary_quote: An async RPC to an Agent addressed with newUniqueId() or idFromString() fails instead of running before initialization.
changes.signal_reason: The async RPC call fails (rejects) instead of running.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Next sentence: 'Address the Agent by name with getAgentByName(), getByName(), or idFromName().'

changes.answer: Callbacks queued with `this.queue()` run later from the alarm loop, so `getCurrentAgent()` inside them returns the agent but not the original `connection` or `request`.
changes.primary_quote: Registered callbacks are user code, so they run inside the host invocation context with the Lifecycle Object available through getCurrentAgent().
changes.signal_reason: getCurrentAgent() still returns; connection/request are just undefined, so code that checks them quietly skips work.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Same page, 'How queue processing works': 'The Lifecycle event loop runs due items in push order, awaiting each callback before starting the next, in a fresh invocation rather than the request that queued them.' lifecycle.md: host context for onAlarm is 'object' only. No docs sentence names connection/request explicitly for queued callbacks.

changes.answer: `useAgent` and `AgentClient` take a `transport` option: "cf-websocket" (default, hibernating) or "capnweb" for a Cap'n Web session with native RPC stubs.
changes.primary_quote: The experimental "capnweb" transport carries protocol frames through a single Cap'n Web RPC session whose root also serves the host's callables natively:
changes.signal_reason: Additive option with an unchanged default; old code keeps the same JSON-over-WebSocket wire.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Preceding sentence: 'The default, "cf-websocket", is a hibernating WebSocket managed by PartySocket.' Also: 'AgentClient accepts the same transport option.' capnweb is experimental and does not hibernate.

changes.answer: `subAgent()` and its siblings are deprecated in favor of `this.dynamicAgents.{get,abort,delete,has,list}`, and facets are positioned as an isolation primitive rather than the way to model many chat sessions.
changes.primary_quote: The subAgent() / hasSubAgent() / listSubAgents() / abortSubAgent() / deleteSubAgent() methods still work and now delegate to the same this.dynamicAgents capability; they are deprecated in place.
changes.signal_reason: Deprecated methods still work unchanged; nothing errors.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Page also: 'Do not use dynamic agents to model an open-ended set of independent peers — many chats, documents, or sessions per user.' and the legacy->capability table (subAgent->dynamicAgents.get, etc.). Quote is inside a markdown blockquote (line prefixes "> " removed when rendered).

changes.answer: `Agent` extends Cloudflare's `DurableObject` directly, with the needed PartyServer runtime vendored into `agents/lifecycle`.
changes.primary_quote: Agent directly extends Cloudflare's DurableObject, so every Agent is a globally addressable, single-threaded compute instance with durable KV/SQLite storage.
changes.signal_reason: Ordinary Agent subclasses run unchanged; assumptions of PartyServer inheritance (e.g. instanceof Server) quietly stop holding, though calls to PartyServer-only methods would throw.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Docs also: 'Each Agent composes a Lifecycle instance.' Source index.ts: 'export class Agent<...> extends DurableObject<Env>'. The 'vendored PartyServer runtime' detail is stated only in the changelog; docs say Agent composes the Lifecycle from agents/lifecycle, and partyserver is no longer a dependency in package.json. lifecycle.md: 'Deprecated name headers and bootstrap methods are not supported.'

changes.answer: `useAgentChat` throttles UI updates to every 50ms by default; pass `throttle: false` to render every chunk or a number to change the interval.
changes.primary_quote: export const DEFAULT_CHAT_THROTTLE_MS = 50;
changes.signal_reason: Changed default: old code runs and simply renders less often.
changes.notes: Not in the docs; source at the tag. chat/react.tsx useAgentChat option JSDoc: 'Milliseconds to coalesce chat state updates before re-rendering, defaulting to 50.' ... 'Pass `false` to render every chunk as it arrives.' experimental_throttle remains as a deprecated alias (resolveChatThrottleMs: throttle ?? experimental_throttle ?? 50).

changes.answer: A scheduled callback's second argument is the parsed `Schedule` object.
changes.primary_quote: method as (payload: unknown, schedule: Schedule<unknown>) => unknown
changes.signal_reason: Old code that JSON.parse()d the raw row's string payload now throws a SyntaxError on the parsed value (other raw-row field reads just return undefined).
changes.notes: Docs show the (payload, schedule: Schedule<...>) shape only in the Scheduler example; the Agent callback resolver in src/index.ts at the tag calls methods with (payload, schedule). schedules/types.ts: 'named handlers receiving the parsed payload and the schedule that fired.' The raw row type ScheduleStorageRow has payload: string.

changes.answer: `agents/schedules` exports `Scheduler`, a Lifecycle capability for delayed, dated, cron and interval callbacks that any Durable Object can use, with typed `set()`/`every()`.
changes.primary_quote: Scheduler is a reusable Lifecycle capability. A plain Lifecycle Object can install it without extending Agent:
changes.signal_reason: Additive: this.schedule() keeps working and delegates to this.scheduler.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Example imports { Scheduler, type Schedule } from "agents/schedules"; 'set() and every() create schedules typed against that registration'. Marked Experimental; Agent's this.schedule() methods are stable. The Durable Object must install a Lifecycle (Lifecycle.install(this).use(...)).

changes.answer: `MCPClientManager` gets storage from the Lifecycle it is installed on; the `storage` option was removed, so standalone construction with explicit DurableObjectStorage is not supported.
changes.primary_quote: MCPClientManager is a lifecycle capability. A class can extend the platform DurableObject directly and install the manager without extending Agent:
changes.signal_reason: Passing `storage` is a type error, and a manager not installed on a Lifecycle has no storage to use.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Example: new MCPClientManager("my-object", "1.0.0") then Lifecycle.install(this).use(this.mcp). Source at tag: MCPClientManagerOptions has only env and createAuthProvider; storage is read via this.lifecycle.storage. Source at tag agents@0.27.0 packages/agents/src/mcp/client/index.ts: MCPClientManagerOptions has only env and createAuthProvider; storage comes from this.lifecycle.storage.

changes.answer: `wrapAISDK()` from `agents/observability/ai` is the only AI SDK tracing integration for both v6 and v7; `createAISDKTelemetry()` was removed.
changes.primary_quote: wrapAISDK supports AI SDK v6 and v7. It instruments generateText, streamText, generateObject, and streamObject.
changes.signal_reason: Importing the removed createAISDKTelemetry export fails.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Next sentence: 'You do not need to register a telemetry integration for Agents tracing on AI SDK v7.' createAISDKTelemetry does not appear anywhere in the docs or downloaded src at the tag.

changes.answer: `createMcpHandler` accepts a factory returning a v2 `McpServer`/`Server` from `@modelcontextprotocol/server` and serves stateless MCP with legacy compatibility; `createLegacyMcpHandler` remains for SDK v1 servers.
changes.primary_quote: createMcpHandler requires a factory so concurrent Worker requests receive isolated server instances. A function input is always treated as an SDK v2 factory.
changes.signal_reason: Passing an SDK v1 server still works through a deprecated overload that only logs a migration warning.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Same page: 'Passing an SDK v1 server directly to createMcpHandler still forwards to this API for compatibility, but that overload is deprecated, emits a migration warning, and is removed in the next major release.' Import createMcpHandler from "agents/mcp/server"; @modelcontextprotocol/server pinned 2.0.0.

changes.answer: The Agents MCP client first probes with `server/discover` (stateless MCP, 2026-07-28) and falls back to the `initialize` handshake for older servers.
changes.primary_quote: It uses server/discover with Stateless servers and falls back to the initialize handshake on the same connection for Legacy Streamable HTTP, SSE, and RPC servers.
changes.signal_reason: Negotiation is automatic with a fallback; old client code and old servers keep working without errors.
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). Preceding sentence: 'Agents uses the MCP v2 client and automatically negotiates the protocol version for every connection.'

changes.answer: agents, @cloudflare/ai-chat and @cloudflare/codemode support both AI SDK v6 and v7 (`ai@^6 || ^7`, `@ai-sdk/react@^3 || ^4`); AI SDK v5 is not supported. @cloudflare/think now requires `ai@^7` only.
changes.primary_quote: The current agents and @cloudflare/ai-chat packages support AI SDK v6 and v7, not v5.
changes.signal_reason: Installing AI SDK v5 per the stale answer fails npm peer-dependency resolution (ERESOLVE).
changes.notes: Quote rendered from markdown (backticks/link syntax/emphasis stripped, wrapped lines joined). package.json peerDependencies at the tag: agents "ai": "^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0", "@ai-sdk/react": "^3.0.0 || ^4.0.0"; ai-chat and codemode same ai range; packages/think/package.json (0.20.1) peer "ai": "^7.0.0" and "@ai-sdk/react": "^4.0.0", so the original claim that think supports v6 is wrong at this tag.

changes.answer: A test fails if an async assertion (such as expect(...).resolves) is not awaited.
changes.primary_quote: Asynchronous assertions, like resolves, rejects and toMatchFileSnapshot, now fail the test if they are not awaited.
changes.signal_reason: An un-awaited expect(...).resolves/.rejects that passed with a warning in v4 now fails the test, with the error pointing at the assertion.
changes.notes: The API page https://vitest.dev/api/expect (resolves/rejects WARNING) agrees: "If the assertion is not awaited, the test will be marked as "failed" at the end of the test." That sentence has no symbol, so the quote is from the migration guide. Also applies to rejects and toMatchFileSnapshot.

changes.answer: Vitest 5 no longer searches parent directories for a config file.
changes.primary_quote: When an explicit --config option is not provided, Vitest looks for vitest.config.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs} first and vite.config.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs} second in the project root. If no config file is found, Vitest will run without one.
changes.signal_reason: Running vitest from a subdirectory no longer finds the parent's config; Vitest runs without a config (no error) and tests run with default settings.
changes.notes: The migration guide (https://vitest.dev/guide/migration) says it directly: "Vitest no longer searches parent directories for config files." and suggests `vitest --config ../vitest.config.ts` with --dir. The quote is two sentences from the config page.

changes.answer: Vitest 5 bundles its own runner and no longer depends on @vitest/runner. The package is deprecated (there is no 5.x release; the 4.x line gets security fixes only) and does not share state with Vitest 5, so use the runner APIs exported from `vitest` (for example `TestRunner`).
changes.primary_quote: The following packages are deprecated as of this release. They will no longer receive feature updates, but security fixes will continue to be backported: @vitest/runner
changes.signal_reason: vitest 5 no longer installs @vitest/runner, so `import ... from '@vitest/runner'` fails to resolve unless the 4.x package is added by hand (and then it does not share state with Vitest 5).
changes.notes: "Not published anymore" overstates it: npm still has @vitest/runner (dist-tag latest 4.1.11, published 2026-08-18, after the v5 betas; last 5.x is 5.0.0-beta.4) and it is not npm-deprecated. vitest@5.0.3 dependencies no longer list @vitest/runner (4.1.11 did); packages/runner is gone from the repo at tag v5.0.0 (404). The quote is the migration guide's sentence plus the first list item that follows it (the line break between them is normalized to a space). No other docs page names @vitest/runner. Same section: vitest/runners entrypoint removed, use TestRunner from vitest.

changes.answer: The WebdriverIO provider was not removed. @vitest/browser-webdriverio (import { webdriverio }, used as test.browser.provider: webdriverio()) moved out of the core repo and is now community maintained in the vitest-community organization; version 5.0.0 is published and works with Vitest 5.
changes.primary_quote: The WebdriverIO provider (@vitest/browser-webdriverio) is maintained by the Vitest community in the vitest-community organization, separately from the core Vitest packages.
changes.signal_reason: Nothing breaks: existing @vitest/browser-webdriverio imports and config keep working on Vitest 5; only who maintains it changed.
changes.notes: https://vitest.dev/guide/browser/webdriverio redirects (301) to /config/browser/webdriverio. npm: @vitest/browser-webdriverio latest 5.0.0, repository github.com/vitest-community/vitest-webdriverio; vitest@5.0.3 lists it as an optional peer (^5.0.0-beta.5 || >=5.0.0). Migration guide: "The @vitest/browser-webdriverio provider has been moved to the vitest-community organization." The "Remove webdriverio package" headline meant removing it from the core monorepo.

changes.answer: toHaveTextContent now matches strictly; use the new toMatchTextContent for partial matching.
changes.primary_quote: The browser-mode toHaveTextContent matcher now validates that an element's text content is exactly equal to the expected string instead of performing a partial, case-sensitive match.
changes.signal_reason: A partial match like toHaveTextContent('Error') against 'Error!' now fails the assertion, and RegExp arguments are no longer accepted.
changes.notes: API page https://vitest.dev/api/browser/assertions: "This matcher allows you to validate that an element's text matches provided string exactly." and "If you wish to perform a partial check or do a case-sensitive match, use toMatchTextContent instead." (neither contains toHaveTextContent, so the quote is from the migration guide). Applies to browser-mode expect.element; RegExp support moved to toMatchTextContent.

changes.answer: The blob reporter and --merge-reports use .vitest/blob/ by default.
changes.primary_quote: Collect the results stored in .vitest/blob/ directory from each machine and merge them with --merge-reports option:
changes.signal_reason: Blob files are written to a different directory without any error; CI steps that upload or read .vitest-reports/ quietly pick up nothing.
changes.notes: Reporters page https://vitest.dev/guide/reporters: "By default, stores all results in .vitest/blob/ folder, but can be overridden with --outputFile or --outputFile.blob flags." Part of a wider move to a single .vitest/ artifact root (html, json, junit and attachments defaults also moved).

changes.answer: In browser mode, locators match text exactly by default (locators.exact is true).
changes.primary_quote: Defaults to browser.locators.exact, which is true by default.
changes.signal_reason: A substring locator such as getByText('Hello') no longer finds 'Hello, World', so actions and expect.element fail with element-not-found (only .query()/.elements() return null/[] quietly).
changes.notes: Config page https://vitest.dev/config/browser/locators: browser.locators.exact, Type boolean, Default true, "When set to true, locators match text exactly by default, requiring a full, case-sensitive match." Set browser.locators.exact: false or pass { exact: false } per call to restore substring matching.

changes.answer: In `-t` / testNamePattern, nested suite and test names are joined with `>`.
changes.primary_quote: For example, the test below has the full name math > adds, so it is matched by -t 'math > adds' or -t adds:
changes.signal_reason: A pattern spanning segments with a space (-t 'math adds') still runs but matches nothing, so the intended tests are skipped instead of run.
changes.notes: Preceding sentence on the same page: "The pattern is matched against the test's full name: the enclosing suite names and the test name joined with ' > ' (the same string shown in the reporter output)." The separator is ' > ' (with spaces). Patterns matching a single segment are unaffected.

changes.answer: Inline projects in `test.projects` inherit the root config by default.
changes.primary_quote: This is controlled by the extends option, which is enabled by default since Vitest 5.0:
changes.signal_reason: Root plugins, aliases and setupFiles are now applied to inline projects (arrays merged) without any error, changing how their tests run.
changes.notes: Preceding sentence: "Projects defined with an inline configuration inherit all options from the root-level configuration." Set extends: false to opt out. name and projects are never inherited, globalSetup is not inherited from the root config, and projects referenced as config files or directories still do not inherit.

changes.answer: expect.poll fails when the polled function does not resolve within the timeout.
changes.primary_quote: expect.poll now rejects when its callback, or the polled assertion, does not settle within timeout.
changes.signal_reason: A poll whose callback or assertion settles late now fails with "expect.poll() function didn't resolve in time." (or "assertion didn't resolve in time.").
changes.notes: API page https://vitest.dev/api/expect (poll): "The timeout applies to the whole polling operation, including pending callback and async matcher execution." and the callback receives an AbortSignal aborted at the timeout. The stale side is slightly off: in v4 a late-resolving callback could still pass, rather than waiting forever.

changes.answer: Calling hoisted methods such as vi.mock outside the module's top level now throws an error.
changes.primary_quote: vi.mock, vi.unmock, and vi.hoisted are hoisted to the top of the file and run before any surrounding code. Calling them inside a function, block, or describe/test callback previously only logged a warning. Vitest 5.0 now throws, because the call does not execute where it is written:
changes.signal_reason: vi.mock/vi.unmock/vi.hoisted nested in a describe, test, hook or block now throws at transform time ("... was defined outside of the module's top level scope").
changes.notes: The quote is three consecutive sentences (the third states the throw). Source at tag v5.0.0, packages/mocker/src/node/hoistMocks.ts, builds the message "defined outside of the module's top level scope:" and does `throw new Error(message)` (skipped when import.meta.vitest is used). vi.doMock/vi.doUnmock may still be called anywhere. Caution: https://vitest.dev/api/vi still says "The call to vi.mock is hoisted, so it doesn't matter where you call it." (stale docs text).

changes.answer: Vitest 5 adds `vi.when()` for argument-conditional mock behavior.
changes.primary_quote: vi.when takes a spy and lets you define argument-specific behaviors.
changes.signal_reason: Additive API: code written without vi.when (mockImplementation with argument checks) keeps working unchanged.
changes.notes: API page https://vitest.dev/api/vi has "vi.when 5.0.0+": when(spy, { onUnmatched }) with .calledWith(...args).thenReturn/thenThrow/thenResolve/thenReject (and *Once); unmatched calls pass through to the original implementation by default.

changes.answer: The `--repeats` CLI option reruns tests a given number of times.
changes.primary_quote: Repeat every test a specific number of times regardless of the result. A test that uses the repeats test option takes precedence over this value.
changes.signal_reason: Additive option: existing per-test repeats keep working and take precedence; nothing errors.
changes.notes: Symbol is the option name: CLI --repeats <number> (guide/cli), config repeats. Config page lists repeats: Type number, Default 0, CLI --repeats=<number>; guide/cli lists "CLI: --repeats <number>". The docs sentence has "repeats" but not the flag; the Vitest 5 blog (https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-5) says: "The new --repeats CLI option repeats every test a given number of times regardless of the result, which is useful for hunting flaky tests." Also available as the global config option repeats.

changes.answer: `-p` is shorthand for `--project`.
changes.primary_quote: The --project filter is aware of the hierarchy, and it now has a -p shorthand:
changes.signal_reason: Additive alias: --project keeps working unchanged.
changes.notes: The CLI reference https://vitest.dev/guide/cli#project shows it only as the 25-character cell "CLI: -p, --project <name>" (below the 40-character minimum), so the quote is from the official Vitest 5 announcement on vitest.dev. Source at tag v5.0.0 (packages/vitest/src/node/cli/cli-config.ts) has `project: { shorthand: 'p', ... }`.

changes.answer: `vitest list` collects tests by static parsing by default instead of running files.
changes.primary_quote: Since Vitest 5, vitest list parses test files statically instead of running them to collect tests.
changes.signal_reason: vitest list still prints a list, but tests generated at runtime (loops, dynamic names) can be missing or named differently, without an error.
changes.notes: Next sentence: "Pass --no-static-parse to run the files instead." Concurrency is set with --static-parse-concurrency (default os.availableParallelism()).
